diagnostics.message: google_org_policy_custom_constraint.constraint creates org-policy custom constraints (needs orgpolicy.policyAdmin), but it has no ordering edge to the org IAM bindings. The resources that consume it (google_org_policy_policy.default) already wait on google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative/.bindings and google_organization_iam_member.bindings precisely so that permissions granted by this module in the same apply exist first; the constraint itself does not, so it can fail with a 403 on a first apply that also grants the runner's orgpolicy role. It should depend on the IAM bindings the same way google_org_policy_policy.default does.

google_logging_organization_settings.default mutates organization-level logging configuration (and can disable the _Default sink), which requires logging admin permissions. Its sibling google_logging_organization_sink.sink already declares depends_on on google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative/.bindings and google_organization_iam_member.bindings so that roles granted by this module land first; the settings resource has no such edge and can fail with a 403 on a first apply that grants the logging role in the same module call.

google_logging_organization_exclusion.logging-exclusion creates organization-level logging exclusions, which require logging admin permissions, but it does not wait on the module's IAM bindings. The other org-level logging resource in the same file (google_logging_organization_sink.sink) explicitly depends on google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative/.bindings and google_organization_iam_member.bindings for exactly this reason, so the exclusion should too, or the first apply can race the role grant it provides.

google_organization_iam_audit_config.default configures organization-level data access audit logs, an org logging-admin operation, but it has no ordering edge to the IAM bindings created in the same module. Every other org-config writer in this module (sink, tag keys, org policies, PAM entitlements, contacts) waits on google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative/.bindings and google_organization_iam_member.bindings so module-granted roles exist first; the audit config should depend on them as well.

google_scc_management_organization_security_health_analytics_custom_module.scc_organization_custom_module writes organization-level Security Command Center configuration (securitycenter.settingsAdmin / SCC module enablement), but it depends only on var.organization_id. If this module grants the applying principal its SCC/security roles through its own IAM bindings, the custom modules can be created before the grant is effective and fail with a 403. It should depend on google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative (and the sibling .bindings / google_organization_iam_member.bindings), matching the pattern used by sink, tag keys, org policies and PAM entitlements.
